Kashem's old radio still reminds the days of '71
2014-12-14T00:00:00+06:00 | Ahmed Humayun Kabir Topu, Pabna
https://www.thedailystar.net/kashems-old-radio-still-reminds-the-days-of-71-55183

Octogenarian Abul Kashem Mollah of Rooppur village in Ishwardi upazila under the district still holds his decades old three brand radio as a prized possession as it helped the locals to hear the BBC news at his tea stall during the turbulent days of the Liberation War.

"Many people thronged Kashem's tea stall to hear the BBC news as they were eager to know about the progress of the Liberation War. The spot, mostly surrounded by jungles, gradually developed into a busy market. Locals call it BBC Bazar,” said freedom fighter Md Rashidullah, a residence of Rooppur village.

In early December of 1971, Pakistan occupation army guided by their local collaborators raided Kashem's tea stall, beat him mercilessly and broke the radio.

After the independence, Kashem got the radio repaired.

Kashem, who could not participate in the armed fight during the Liberation War due to family obligations, often helped the freedom fighters in different ways.

“The people from Rooppur, Pakshey, Sahapur and adjoining villages came to my shop to hear the BBC news that seemed authentic during the Liberation War. They also heard programmes of Swadhin Bangla Betar Kendra. I got the honour of a freedom fighter as my radio helped to keep freedom-loving people's morale high.

"I have reached the twilight hours of my life. My beloved wife passed away. Sons and daughters are busy with their own families. Now I want the historic radio to be preserved in the museum," said Kashem, now 85.

Despite suffering from old-age complications, he often makes time to narrate the memories of the Liberation War to the young people.
